metric_protocol: pooled five-fold out-of-fold evaluation, 3 training seeds (42, 1, 2), fold partition fixed at the seed-42 split

architecture.parity_rule: same encoder, same graph, same folds, same seeds on every rung; the loop additionally trains a classification head on the semantic embeddings
architecture.description: shared canonical architecture; the loop consults the per-fold trained LLM head, the LLM rung and AGAF keep the whitened prototype encoder

headline: With the trained head as consultant the loop is separated above AGAF and above the GNN on BOTH datasets — the first separated ladder step this project has measured — and is NOT separated from the head alone on either. The shape now agrees across datasets; the level does not and never did.
notes: Absolute macro-F1 levels are not interchangeable across datasets because eval-class counts differ (UNSW 10 vs ToN 8).
The ladder holds on UNSW-NB15 (GNN<LLM<AGAF<Loop by point estimate; loop-vs-AGAF gap CI still touches zero, P=0.778).

The ladder does NOT hold on ToN-IoT, but not for the reason it used to: AGAF now sits BELOW the GNN rung (P=0.0005), and the loop is the TOP rung on ToN, significantly above AGAF (P=1.000). The regression is AGAF's, not the loop's.

Trained-head LLM-only baselines are reported separately in results/{unsw_nb15,ton_iot}_head_baseline.json. Those baseline files were generated 2026-08-20, on the v1 encoding and pre-fusion-fix architecture, and have not been re-run on v2 — treat their exact values as approximate until re-verified, though on both datasets the qualitative finding (trained head beats the full loop) is expected to still hold given the loop's v2 gains are modest relative to the baseline's margin.

Schema 4 re-runs both datasets on the v2 edge-attribute encoding (log1p+Z-score continuous columns, learned embeddings for protocol/port) with the loop-fusion fairness fix (fusion_dim matches AGAF's projection dim; prototype path uses the same confidence gate as the trained-head path). Schema 3 was produced on the v1 encoding.
2026-09-06: superseded single-seed schema 3/5 contracts with 3-seed condition-A measurements; see each contract's supersedes block.

The head-alone rung is the loop's own consultant standing alone. It carries the highest mean on both datasets. Any statement of the loop's gain over AGAF or the GNN must be accompanied by the loop-vs-head_alone interval, which includes zero on both datasets with an unstable sign.
Knob selection curves for the head consultant are flat within noise on both datasets; ToN's injection_scale sits on the upper range boundary.

supersedes.reason: The loop's semantic consultant is the per-fold trained head on CySecBERT embeddings (llm_head_logits.pt, in-fold on train/val, out-of-fold on test; the cross-fitted variant was measured worse, 2026-09-07). The LLM rung and AGAF keep the embedding-only whitened prototype: the semantic branch is compared as an encoder, the loop is the proposed system. The head alone is reported as the strongest LLM-only baseline in every table. Architecture parity rule: same encoder, same graph, same folds, same seeds on every rung; the loop additionally trains a classification head on the semantic embeddings.
supersedes.headline: No rung comparison is separated on either dataset once training-seed variance is included. Orderings by 3-seed mean: UNSW LLM < GNN < Loop < AGAF; ToN LLM < AGAF < GNN < Loop. Absolute levels are not comparable across datasets (10 vs 8 scored classes); only the shape is.
